historical_reviews.v3_1: The Master Get/GET method conflicts with an enable action; the review preserves the conflict and treats remote-media exposure as a scoped security-state transition.

original_test_intent: Enable AMI OEM remote-media capability, or inspect that capability, with the preserved source ambiguously using Get/GET against a state-changing action URI.
original_method: After resolving method and OEM semantics, enable remote media once for an explicitly approved Manager/device scope and bounded window, verify only the intended exposure, then disable it and prove the security/media/host baseline is restored.
manual_activity: Resolve GET versus POST, define whether enablement is global, per Manager or per device, approve allowed clients/image sources and duration, and supply the exact DisableRMedia/restore contract.
required_inputs: Canonical action URI and exact payload
Scope model and persistence across session/BMC reboot
Baseline remote-media feature and access-control state
Allowed management networks/clients and image sources
Trusted TLS and privileged credential handle
safety_requirements: Never run the source GET as an action
Never guess OEM fields or scope
Do not enable globally when narrower scope is approved
No unapproved image source or network exposure
No automatic retry after uncertain completion
Require verified disable/restore and exposure closure
agent_execution_scope: Bind BMC, Manager and firmware identity
Read OEM action metadata and current exposure state
Map affected devices, interfaces, roles and clients
Verify intended enablement and reject broader exposure
Audit feature, network, media and host state against baseline
engineer_actions: Approve scope, duration, allowed clients/sources and security impact

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: POST fits enable-action semantics, but it materially changes the Master GET and lacks AMI scope, payload, persistence, network exposure and disable details; generic revert is insufficient.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: With the approved OEM contract, issue one exact POST for the narrowest authorized scope/window, verify exposure, then execute the documented disable/restore and prove no listener, permission or media state remains changed.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Manager-scoped OEM action and 15/10 timing remain; no scope, payload, duration, permitted source or cleanup is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat remote-media enablement as a temporary privileged capability lease with explicit scope, expiry and verified revocation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the GET/POST conflict explicit and adds exposure mapping, bounded duration, security approval, post-disable listener/access checks and one-shot ambiguity handling.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Covers enable/disable state and exposure only; it does not prove image insertion, transfer performance or boot behavior.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A successful disable response may leave sessions, listeners or cached authorization active; recovery must verify observable exposure rather than only a Boolean field.

project_override_considerations: If EnableRMedia is a global BMC feature despite its Manager URI, approval must cover every affected VirtualMedia device and management interface. A vendor-defined automatic timeout may supplement but not replace explicit cleanup verification.
expected_evidence: AMI schema, canonical action target and exact redacted payload
Pre-state feature, device, role, network/listener and host boot evidence
Approved scope, clients/sources, duration and maintenance window
Enabled-state and exposure checks showing no scope expansion

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item and Procedure say Get and send GET, while the URI is an AMI EnableRMedia action and DeepSeek/GPT V2 require POST. A read and a privileged capability enablement have materially different effects, so this is a source conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The OEM contract, scope, approval and disable verification are identifiable prerequisites, so the case is REQUIRES rather than irreducibly BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Reframes a misleading GET as a temporary, auditable security capability change whose scope and revocation must be proven, not assumed.
independent_technical_reasoning: EnableRMedia can widen the attack and operational surface even if no image is inserted: it may expose services, permit remote image attachment or alter role permissions across multiple devices. Therefore the core oracle is not merely an enabled flag but a before/during/after exposure map tied to a narrow time window. Because OEM scope and persistence are unknown, the AMI contract is mandatory. A timeout cannot be retried blindly; read-only inspection determines whether enablement occurred. Cleanup is complete only when the feature, listeners/sessions, media state and host behavior match the baseline.
